name: core.openwop.workflows.support
description: Real-work workflow pack (RFC 0013, ADR 0190) — the Customer Support cluster, the #1 surveyed agent use case the gallery previously had zero templates for: KB-grounded answering, email triage (draft-only — the human sends), customer-ticket routing, sentiment/brand-risk escalation, and CSAT follow-up. Authored entirely over node typeIds shipped with this host (feature.kb + core.ai.chatCompletion + core.flow.if + core.chat.approvalGate + core.email.draft + core.openwop.connectors.ticket-create + core.openwop.integration.*). Every external SEND waits on a human approval gate (core.email.draft creates a draft and never sends — the draft itself is the human gate). Distinct from core.openwop.workflows.it-support: that pack routes IT incidents by severity; this one serves customer-facing support (intent, queues, CSAT). All tenant values are run parameters (replay-deterministic).
author: openwop

chains.label: Knowledge-Base Support Agent
chains.description: Answer a customer question grounded ONLY in your knowledge base, with citations and a stated confidence. Confident answers are delivered as a notification; low-confidence ones route to a human-approved Slack escalation instead of guessing.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

orgId.description: The org whose knowledge base is searched. Must be the same org the collection belongs to, or nothing is found.

collectionId.description: The KB collection id to search (create via the Knowledge feature or knowledge-sync).

config.systemPrompt: You are a support agent. Answer the customer question using ONLY the retrieved knowledge-base passages — cite each passage you rely on. If the KB does not cover the question, say so plainly. End with a line 'CONFIDENCE: high' or 'CONFIDENCE: low' (low when the KB coverage is partial or absent). Question: {{params.question}}

answer.description: The KB-grounded answer with citations and confidence, or the escalation note.

chains.label: Support Email Triage & Reply Draft
chains.description: Classify an inbound support email (intent, urgency, suggested queue) and draft a reply INTO YOUR DRAFTS FOLDER — this workflow creates a draft and never sends; you review and send from your own mailbox. The draft is the human gate.

emailText.description: The inbound support email body (with subject if available).

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: You are a support triage specialist. Classify this inbound email: intent (question / bug / billing / refund / feedback / other), urgency (low / normal / high), and the suggested queue. Then outline the key points a reply must address. Email: {{params.emailText}}
Write a {{params.replyTone}} reply to the customer email, addressing every key point from the triage. Do not invent policy or promises — where information is missing, say the team will follow up.

triage.description: The classification plus the drafted reply saved to your mail drafts.

chains.label: Customer Ticket Routing & Prioritization
chains.description: Classify an inbound customer request (team, priority, first-response suggestion), create a ticket in your ticketing system, and notify the owning queue. Customer-support routing — for IT incident severity routing use the IT pack's Incident Triage.

ticketProject.description: Project/queue key for the created ticket.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: You are a support-ops router. For this customer request, decide: owning team (billing / technical / account / product), priority (P1–P4 with rationale), and a one-line first-response suggestion. Request: {{params.requestText}}

routing.description: The classification and the created ticket reference.

chains.label: Sentiment & Brand-Risk Watch
chains.description: Score an inbound message (review, social mention, reply) for sentiment and brand risk. Normal messages are logged as a notification; high-risk ones route to a human-approved Slack escalation. A watch on what customers say ABOUT you — inbox triage lives in Support Email Triage.

message.description: The inbound message, review, or mention to score.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: You are a CX analyst. Score this message: sentiment (positive / neutral / negative), brand risk (none / low / high — high means churn threat, public escalation, legal or safety language), and the single best next action. Message: {{params.message}}

assessment.description: The sentiment/risk assessment and the action taken.

chains.label: CSAT Follow-up Survey
chains.description: After a ticket resolves, draft a short personalized customer-satisfaction (CSAT) survey email and send it — behind a human approval. When a low score comes back later, run Customer Ticket Routing on it to open a manager review.

resolutionSummary.description: Short summary of the resolved ticket (what was fixed, for whom).
